html:
The Battle of Kwajalein was fought in early 1944, when US forces took the atoll of Kwajalein, the hub of Japan's defences in the Marshall Islands, in a few days.

Japan had ruled the Marshalls since 1914 under a League of Nations mandate. Learning from Tarawa, the Americans pounded the islets first, and losses were far lower.

After the war the Marshalls came under US trusteeship. Kwajalein became a missile test range, and Marshallese landowners were moved to the crowded islet of Ebeye, a source of grievance. Nearby atolls were used for the nuclear tests at Bikini and Castle Bravo. See Pacific War.
